end.summary:
Practised placing BCE and CE dates on a timeline.
Discussed archaeological remains, inscriptions, texts, and oral traditions as historical sources.
Aarav identified that BCE dates move left and count down toward 1 BCE; CE dates move right.
Aarav initially treated written books as the only source and one inscription as fully reliable; this was not fully corrected by the end.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised BCE/CE timeline direction and how different sources reveal different parts of the past. Aarav used the idea of checking another inscription to question a single written account, which was a useful method. They still needed more support to explain how objects and bones provide evidence, and this was not fully corrected by the end. At home, ask Aarav to sort examples—pottery, bones, inscriptions, books, and oral stories—and say one thing each can tell us.
